items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I couldn’t believe that Roy Eldridge just wanted to hang out you know, [laughs] not when I was a kid.

ctx.x: Did you have much contact with Ellington and Billy Strayhorn?

Never. Not even when I played opposite them, I was too much in awe of Ellington, in fact I didn’t have contact with a lot of people ‘cause I was pitifully shy. I really was, up until about ten, fifteen years ago, I would never get to close to people ‘cause, I don’t know I was just shy. And I missed a lot, and I missed meeting a lot of people because of it and I realized, I guess I finally grew up and got – I realized how stupid it was. But that happens you know, I see people act that way sometimes around people,…
There’s a wonderful quote, that Gene Lees mentioned that you said that, “the Ellington band was either sounded wonderful or terrible but it was never mediocre.”
